packages.label: יָד הַגְּדוֹלָה וְהִסְתַּפְּקוּת
packages.reason: Both concepts express the same essential reality: divine infinite provision. The 'Great Hand' (יָד הַגְּדוֹלָה) is God's boundless capacity to provide — proven by the verse 'הֲיַד ה' תִּקְצָר' (Is God's hand too short? — Numbers 11:23). Contentment/sufficiency (הִסְתַּפְּקוּת) is the state of satiated abundance that proceeds from that infinite divine provision. The Rebbe equates them directly: 'יָד הַגְּדוֹלָה הוּא בְּחִינַת הִסְתַּפְּקוּת'. They are two faces of the same divine quality — inexhaustible adequacy. The one is the metaphysical/divine dimension (God's hand that never falls short), the other is the experiential/human dimension (the feeling of having enough). Together they form the positive domain of this Torah: the blessing that flows to the one who gives maaser (tithe).
